S15.01.note: The model name is data, so no fixed label is shown; the panel title is the only fixed word found.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Look at the composer at the bottom of the screen and find the model button; note the model name shown on it.
Tap that button to open the panel titled Models.
Pick a different model, close the panel, and check the composer shows the new model's name.
S15.01.where: New chat screen > the composer at the bottom > the model button beside the send button (its name shows the current model); tap it to open the Models panel

S15.02.note: Each row shows the provider as the fallback guidance text when no other description exists (model.provider in ComposerFooter.tsx).
steps: Open a new chat and tap the model button in the composer.
In the Models panel, tap All models.
Look at the row of developers under the search box, under the label Model developers.
Open a model row and compare the provider shown with the developer rail.
S15.02.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > model developer rail

S15.03.note: Grouping is built in ModelCatalogue.tsx (groups by line label); I did not confirm a visible group heading for each family.
steps: Open the Models panel from the composer and tap All models.
Look at the list: versions of one model line should sit together.
Tap the About button on a model row and find the Family line in the card.
Compare the family shown with the other versions listed next to it.
S15.03.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > model developer rail, and the About card's Family line

steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Tap the box with the placeholder Search models.
Type part of a model name.
Check that the list shrinks to matching models, and that No models match appears when nothing fits.
S15.04.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > Search models box

S15.05.note: The code spells it Favourites; the rail count shows how many are starred.
steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Tap the star button on a model row; its label changes to Remove <model> from favourites.
Tap the Favourites rail entry.
Check the starred model is listed on its own.
S15.05.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > star button on a model row, then the Favourites rail

S15.06.needs: a signed-in account with some past model use
steps: Use two or three different models in chats.
Open the Models panel from the composer and tap All models.
Tap the Recent rail entry.
Check the models you used most recently appear there.
S15.06.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > Recent rail

S15.07.note: The Recommended section appears only when the account is on a paid plan (paidPlan check in ComposerFooter.tsx).
steps: Sign in with a paid plan.
Open the Models panel from the composer.
Look for the section labelled Recommended above the rest of the list.
Compare the models listed there with what Expected says.
S15.07.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > section labelled Recommended

labels.text: Picks the best model for each message

S15.08.needs: a signed-in account; a Free account sees Auto (free) instead
steps: Open the Models panel from the composer.
Find the top row, which shows the guidance text Picks the best model for each message.
Tap it and send a message.
Check the composer label shows Auto and the answer discloses which model was chosen (Auto chose ...).
S15.08.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > top row Auto

S15.09.note: How Settings is opened from the main screen was not traced; the General and Default model labels were found.
steps: Open Settings and tap General.
Find the row labelled Default model.
Open the select and choose a model; the hint under the row says New chats start with this model.
Open a new chat and check the composer shows the chosen model.
Tap the model button in the composer.
In the Models panel, tap a model row.
Check the composer model button now shows that model's name.
Send a message and check the answer is labelled with that model.
S15.10.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > tap a model row

S15.11.note: The guidance line falls back to the provider name when no guidance is defined (ComposerFooter.tsx).
steps: Open the Models panel from the composer.
Read the one-line text under each model name.
Tap the About button on a row to open its card.
Compare the text with the short description in Expected.
S15.11.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > each model row's guidance line, and the About button on a row

S15.12.note: Capability chips filter the list; the per-row icons are capability marks, which I did not trace further.
steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Look at the chips under the search box: Vision, Tools, Search and others.
Tap Audio in or Vision to filter the list.
Check the models shown accept that input.
S15.12.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > Filter by capability chips (Vision, Audio in)

steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Tap the chip Image out.
Check the models shown produce images.
Repeat with Video out and Audio out and compare with Expected.
S15.13.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > Filter by capability chips (Image out, Video out, Audio out)

steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Tap the Tools chip under Filter by capability.
Check that only models with tool support are listed.
Compare with Expected.
S15.14.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > Tools chip

S15.15.note: Values are shown only when the catalogue has a positive number for that model.
steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Tap the About button on a model row.
Find the line Context ceiling and the line Output ceiling in the card.
Compare the numbers with the model's documented context size.
S15.15.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > About button on a model row > Context ceiling

S15.16.note: No visible wording about relative speed (faster or slower) was found in ModelCatalogue.tsx, ComposerFooter.tsx or packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/modelPicker.ts; the only speed text found is the Fast mode toggle (see S15.23). The cited lines are no longer there.

S15.17.note: The row price band is an aria and title text Price band N of M (ComposerFooter.tsx and ModelCatalogue.tsx).
steps: Open the Models panel and tap All models.
Tap the About button on a model row.
Read the lines Typical message and Credits per 1M tokens.
Compare the cost lines with the price band shown on the row.
S15.17.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > All models > About button on a model row > Credits per 1M tokens and Typical message

S15.18.note: The lock text comes from the server row lock; the default text when none is set is Requires upgrade.
steps: Sign in on a Free plan.
Open the Models panel from the composer.
Find a model row marked with a lock; its text shows the plan that unlocks it, and it has an Upgrade button.
Tap What each plan includes to see the plan list.
S15.18.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > a locked model row shows its plan and an Upgrade button

S15.19.needs: a signed-in account; whether a Preview model is listed depends on the catalogue
S15.19.note: The Preview and Experimental words come from the routing package, not the web app; I did not check whether any preview model is in the live catalogue.
steps: Open the Models panel from the composer.
Look for a row carrying a badge: Preview or Experimental.
Also look for the Beta or Coming soon tag on other rows.
Compare the badges shown with Expected.
S15.19.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > a model row with a stage badge (Preview, Experimental) or the Beta or Coming soon tag

S15.20.needs: a model whose retirement date is within 30 days (a test or live catalogue entry)
S15.20.note: The notice only shows inside the 30-day window (DEPRECATION_WARNING_WINDOW_DAYS); outside it nothing shows.
steps: Open the Models panel from the composer.
Look at the status line of each row for the text Leaving on followed by a date.
Compare the date with the retirement date.
Check the row is still selectable before the date passes.
S15.20.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > a model row within 30 days of retirement shows Leaving on <date>

S15.21.needs: a model that is marked unavailable in the live catalogue (may not occur in a normal account)
steps: Open the Models panel from the composer.
Find a row with the text Temporarily unavailable (catalogue) or Unavailable right now (chooser row).
Try to tap that row.
Check the row cannot be chosen and the composer model does not change.
S15.21.where: New chat > composer model button > Models panel > a model row marked Temporarily unavailable or Unavailable right now

S15.22.needs: a reasoning-capable model; a paid plan may be needed for higher levels
S15.22.note: The control is hidden for models without reasoning; the value Off is shown when the slider is off.
steps: Choose a reasoning model from the Models panel.
Look at the composer for the control labelled Reasoning effort.
Tap it and move the slider to another level.
Send a message and check the answer used the chosen level (compare with Expected).
S15.22.where: New chat > pick a reasoning model in the composer model button > the composer control labelled Reasoning effort (its slider shows Off or the level)

S15.23.needs: a model with a fast tier and an account allowed to use it (a paid plan is likely)
S15.23.note: The Fast mode switch is placed inside the same panel as the effort control (located by line position in ComposerFooter.tsx, not by a full trace).
steps: Choose a model that offers faster serving from the Models panel.
Tap the Reasoning effort control in the composer.
Find the switch labelled Fast mode and turn it on; a Fast pill appears.
Read the help text and compare the extra usage with Expected.
S15.23.where: New chat > pick a model that offers a fast tier > the Reasoning effort control > the Fast mode switch

S15.24.note: The length option names come from RESPONSE_LENGTH_OPTIONS in apps/web/features/chat/stores/style-store.ts; I did not read their words.
steps: Tap the Style control in the composer.
Find the heading Response Length and the row of length buttons below it.
Tap a different length and close the panel.
Send the same question and compare answer length with Expected.
S15.24.where: New chat > composer Style control (labelled Style) > Response Length row of buttons

S15.27.needs: the Desktop app; a paid account (the section is hidden on Free); Ollama or LM Studio with a model loaded
S15.27.note: The section appears only when the account is not on the Free plan; the local-runtime dispatcher is apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts.
steps: Start the Desktop app on a paid plan with Ollama or LM Studio running and a model loaded.
Open the Models panel from the composer.
Find the section On this device; if asked, allow Use models on this device.
Pick a local model, send a message and check the composer shows the local model name with the Local badge.
S15.27.where: Desktop app > New chat > composer model button > Models panel > section On this device (Use models on this device; Manage local models)

S15.29.needs: a Free account or a paid account; the model must be one your plan can use
S15.29.note: The choice is saved in the browser's local storage under the key agi-model-store (apps/web/shared/stores/model-store.ts:376), so it is per device, not per account; a tester must reopen the app to confirm. The Desktop shell shows the hosted web app, so a reopen check is the same as in the browser.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Click the model name button under the message box (its label ends in "change model").
In the "Models" list, click a different model such as one shown in the list.
Close the list, press Cmd+R or quit and reopen the Desktop app, then open a new chat.
Compare: the composer still shows the model you picked, as Expected says.
S15.29.where: Composer, model button (shows the model name) > pick a model in the list (under "Models")

labels.text: Could not save the model for this conversation. The previous model remains active.

S15.30.needs: a Free account or a paid account; two chats
S15.30.note: The per-conversation save is wired in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx (handleConversationModelChange, passed as onModelChange); the list confirms the choice only through the saved state, and the error toast names the failure.
steps: Sign in, open an existing chat or start one and send a message.
Click the model name button under the message box.
In the "Models" list, click a different model.
Open a different chat, then come back to this chat.
Compare: this chat still uses the model you picked, while the other chat keeps its own model, as Expected says.
S15.30.where: Open a chat > Composer, model button (ends in "change model") > pick a model in the "Models" list

S15.31.needs: a chat with an answer; a Free account or a paid account
S15.31.note: The menu appears for a reply (not on the user's own message); the check that the chat's model stays the same is inferred from the code path onRegenerateWithModel, not from a visible label.
steps: Open a chat that has at least one answer.
Hover the answer so the action icons appear under it.
Click the "Regenerate response" button.
In the menu, look at the list under "Try again with" and click a different model.
Compare: a new answer appears from that model, and the chat's own model in the model button does not change, as Expected says.
S15.31.where: Chat > under an answer, hover it and click "Regenerate response" (the arrow icon) > "Try again with" list

S15.32.needs: none beyond a Free account or a paid account; a message that has an answer
S15.32.note: The name text comes from getManagedModelPresentationLabel in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/modelInfo.ts; the line is hidden until hover, so a tester must hover before reading it. The text "Answered by" appears only inside a tooltip for on-device answers (MessageBubble.tsx:467), not as a label on the main line.
steps: Open a chat and send a message to get an answer.
Move the mouse over the answer so the line under it appears (it is hidden until hover, or shown by touch on a touch screen).
Read the line under the answer that names the model.
Compare: the name shown is the model that wrote this answer, with "Auto chose" in front when Auto was used, as Expected says.
S15.32.where: Chat > hover an answer from the assistant > small line under the answer that names the model (for example "Auto chose" followed by the model name)

S15.33.needs: a situation where the chosen model fails and another model answers; a tester cannot force this from the menus alone
S15.33.note: The reason text comes from describeFallbackReason in apps/web/lib/chat-fallback-reason.ts and was not read in full; the notice shows only when a substitute answered, so the tester may not reach it on demand.
steps: Start a chat and send a message.
Look under the answer for a grey notice box with the words from the substitution text.
Click "Dismiss" to remove the notice, then send another message if one appears again.
Compare: the notice says a different model answered and gives the reason, and "Dismiss" hides it, as Expected says.
S15.33.where: Chat > under an answer, a grey notice box that says why another model answered (with a "Dismiss" button)

S15.34.needs: a Free account or a paid account; an image file to upload; a model in the list that cannot read images
S15.34.note: The reasons come from evaluateModelCompatibility in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/model-compatibility.ts; the box sits inside the model picker, not as a separate popup, and the exact model that triggers it depends on the account's plan and the list.
steps: Open a new chat and attach an image using the attach control in the message box.
Click the model name button under the message box.
Click a model that cannot read images, if one is listed.
Read the box that says "Switch to" followed by the model name, and the reason under it.
Compare: the box names what will be lost and gives "Switch anyway" and "Keep <your current model>" buttons, as Expected says.
S15.34.where: Composer, model button (ends in "change model") > pick a model that cannot read the current chat (such as a text-only model when an image is attached) > the box that says "Switch to <model name>?"

S15.35.needs: a Free account or a paid account; an image or document file to upload; a model in the list that cannot read it
S15.35.note: The box text differs for free plans ("This free model accepts text only..." or "accepts images only...") and uses "Use Free Auto" instead of "Use Auto"; the box is the same conflict surface as S15.34 and is shown only when the chosen model cannot read the file.
steps: Open a new chat and attach an image or document with the attach control.
Click the model name button and choose a model that cannot read that file type.
Read the box above the message box that starts with "The selected model can't read the attached".
Click "Choose a compatible model" to see the list of models that can read it, or click "Use Auto" to switch.
Compare: you can keep the file by switching to a model that can read it, or remove it with "Remove attachments", as Expected says.
S15.35.where: Composer, a red-grey box above the message box after you attach a file a model cannot read > buttons "Use Auto" or "Choose a compatible model" or "Remove attachments"
